basic.title: Basic Turn
basic.description: Start from the real opening entry, then finish one hand action and one wheel action.

steps.welcome: Seven Hatreds has three victory paths: control 16 regions at New Year, capture an opponent's capital, or reach 3 prestige first.
steps.handLimit: At the start of every turn, check hand limit first. Ming may keep 15 cards; Later Jin and the Mongols may keep 10.
steps.openingEntry: This turn has two parts: one hand action and one wheel action. The current player chooses the order.
steps.handResource: Cards are your resource: events resolve when played, armaments need one extra discard, tactics stay for battle, and silver only pays costs.
steps.selectRegion: This action needs a region first. Click Pidao, then choose Grant Pardon.
steps.pickAction: Choose Grant Pardon. It changes a neighboring enemy troop into Ming control.
steps.payCards: Discard 3 cards first, then resolve Grant Pardon.
steps.actionResult: The board has already changed. The cards you spent have become real map control.
steps.moraleLevel: The number on each troop is both level and morale.
steps.wheelMove: The hand action is done. Now choose one wheel action.
steps.finish: That turn is done: cards changed the map, and the wheel pushed play forward.

attackAndBattle.title: Attack And Battle
attackAndBattle.description: Enter from a real dispatch target state, then see a live battle settlement and post-battle result.

steps.overview: An attack moves first, then settles the battle.
steps.moveEntry: Pick one of the real attack targets.
steps.battleOpen: Read the committed troops, defender, and battle width.
steps.battleResult: Read the result and surviving troops.
steps.retreatAndDefeat: The defeat marker is already up. The loser still has to pay a retreat cost.
steps.finish: This attack is done: target, battle, then post-battle handling.

siege.title: Siege And Occupation
siege.description: See why winning a city battle still leaves a decision between occupation, siege, and withdrawal.

steps.overview: Winning a city battle still leaves a state choice.
steps.defendCity: Settle the city battle first. This is not occupation yet.
steps.cityBattle: Read the committed force, casualties, and remaining defenders.
steps.cityResult: After the battle, decide whether to occupy, besiege, or step back.
steps.besiegeChoice: Besieging keeps pressure on the city but does not change control yet.
steps.finish: A city battle closes with the city's new state.

wheelSharedCost.title: Wheel Cost
wheelSharedCost.description: See what happens when you move 3 spaces: both opponents draw, and the wheel pushes you into the next system.

steps.overview: Wheel movement is never free. The farther you move, the more cards your opponents recover.
steps.drawResult: After moving 3 spaces, both the Mongols and Later Jin each drew 2 cards.
steps.dispatchReady: Once that cost is paid, the wheel also pushes this turn into the attack / dispatch entry.
steps.finish: The wheel decides both which system you enter and how many cards your opponents regain.

diplomacy.title: Diplomacy And Hire
diplomacy.description: Enter a real wheel diplomacy step and see control markers and hired troops resolve together.

steps.overview: Diplomacy changes relations. Hiring changes where new troops appear.
steps.wheelEntry: Push the wheel into Diplomacy / Hire.
steps.chooseTarget: Read which friendly region is projecting influence.
steps.tributeMark: The next step can turn friendly into tribute.
steps.removeMark: Diplomacy can also remove someone else's marker.
steps.hireOnly: After relations are set, place hired troops in a controlled area.
steps.finish: This wheel action changes relations and adds force.

yearAndCharacters.title: Midyear, Characters, And Chronology
yearAndCharacters.description: See Midyear checks, New Year maintenance, chronology scoring, and how a new year reshuffles the game.

steps.overview: When the wheel reaches Midyear and New Year, the year's results settle together.
steps.midyearTax: Read taxes first: which controlled regions gave cards back.
steps.midyearCharacters: Then read character checks and defeat pressure.
steps.advanceNewYear: After Midyear, push on into New Year.
steps.chronologyScore: To take prestige from chronology, the leader must pay cards.
steps.turnOrderRefresh: After chronology, turn order and characters refresh together.
steps.finish: A year end reshuffles resources, characters, and order.

koreaSpecial.title: Korea And Special Map Rules
koreaSpecial.description: Read the map-specific rules around Korea, Hanseong, sea routes, and Shanhaiguan.

steps.overview: Korea, Hanseong, sea routes, and Shanhaiguan all change the rules directly.
steps.koreaRegion: Read Korea first: no population, no hegemony control, but it does produce Korea cards.
steps.waterLimit: Sea routes between anchor regions move at most 2 troops.
steps.shanhaiguan: If Shanhaiguan stands, the border stays narrow; if ruined, it collapses into plain ground.
steps.finish: These map rules directly change scoring, movement, and defense.
